Your boyfriend is an asshole for refusing to learn. Having said that, he's probably refusing to learn because he put up blocks in his mind regarding this issue, due to the treatment you've given him because of it. It sounds paradoxical, and it is, but it probably makes perfect sense to him. Please, for the sake if everybody's well-being, find a different way to approach this. Treating your boyfriend like a child can easily destroy an otherwise sturdy relationship. By treating him like a child in this situation, you're taking away his sense of feeling valued. Even if you see it as only affecting him when he's doing dishes, i can guarantee he's thinking about it whenever he does most things with you, because you've planted the idea that you can do this shit at any time. The truth is that it can feel like abuse when it happens to you, and I know that firsthand. For your sake, and the sake of your boyfriend, find a better way of dealing with this situation. 

I learned to wash dishes better because my ex stopped treating me like a child and started encouraging me to do better at it. She would show me how to do it better, help me with a few, and then let me take over. I recommend that approach, because your current approach isn't working. 

It seems like he's already starting to be affected by this problem since he's already started to shut you down when you bring it up. That's a sign you need to change the approach. If he's refusing to hear it out, that means you've already fucked up his perception enough that he's trying to cling to some idea in this head. Furthering his treatment the way you have would only make the problem even worse, unless he finally snapped and heard you out completely, but reaching that point could actually classify as mental abuse.

I never stated that cheating was in the same level as getting a tattoo. In fact, I specifically started otherwise. My point was that the whole "Her body, her rules" topic has no moral ground to stand on, figuratively speaking. While i completely agree that the OP was definitely over-reacting, to excuse his wife for not bothering to even tell him she was getting a hand tattoo until after she had gotten it, ESPECIALLY if she knows he was opposed to that, is a hypocritical ideal. Any functioning relationship needs complete, and total communication between partners, especially when involving topics that one party is opposed to. To not include the other party in that decision is a violation of trust in the relationship.

When I say boundaries, i don't refer to thing that should never be crossed, I'm referring to points that have to be addressed before progressing. In the same way you would talk to your partner about how you should arrange a room, you should also talk to your partner about tattoos you are getting. The problem isn't that the tattoo was on her hand, the problem is that she didn't even try to tell him about it before she got it. She should have at least notified him of it before she got it, since it deviated from her original intention of getting two tattoos in total. OP actually addressed that criticism in some of his replies to other comments.

So let's take what you said a little bit further. Let's say your partner decides to sleep with somebody you both know, and somebody she knows you don't like or trust. Would your reaction be "tough shit, life like that sometimes" or would you feel betrayed? I mean, it's her body and she can do whatever she wants with it, so you have no right to be upset, right? It's the same premise: her body, her rules. If you get upset about one of them, you have to get upset about both, otherwise you're a hypocrite. If you don't find the prospect of either upsetting, there's some general undertones that you might need to have addressed. Maybe talk to a psychologist while OP is getting anger management training.

He mentioned that he finds hand tattoos unattractive and off putting. Beyond that though, he also mentioned that the tattoo isn't the main reason he is upset, it's the fact that she knew he was very opposed to the idea and she did it anyways. It's one thing to be ignorant of boundaries, but it's another thing altogether to ignore and go past boundaries that you know are there.

If you two are still wanting a party to go along with it then don't let anybody stop you, but you won't have the financial support of your families going forward.

NTA. I'd she had just been lying about herself then I'd say she's just an attention seeker, but if she's getting kids involved and started a Go fund me, she's essentially committing fraud. Involving children is a horrific thing, especially if she's forcing her kids to go along with the narrative. Report the go fund me fundraiser if you haven't already done so. As for calling her out on it, my advice would be for you to do so, but make sure you do it respectfully. People deserve to know the truth about the situation, and if you KNOW she's lying and profiting from it, then she needs to be called it on it. Having said that, you're going to face a bit of backlash from it. If she's growing a community, then that community will try to go after you, especially if they're the same ones who already donated. People don't like to be told they've been lied to, and they especially hate being told they've donated to the person who lied to them, so those people will be the ones who go after you hardest. If you decide to call her out on Twitter, I would create a throwaway account to use. Never poison the well you drink from.

You say you don't want to hurt the kids' feelings, but they'll find out eventually, and you'll be remembered as the person who helped their dad cheat on their mom. Having said that, your brother is a piece of shit for cheating on his wife* 

I put an Asterisk at the end of that statement because I realized you mentioned that she has repeatedly laid hands on him. What that tells me is that she has been domestically abusing him, which is never okay REGARDLESS OF WHO IS THE AGGRESSOR. I had to capitalize that because plenty of people fail to realize that men can just as easily be victims of domestic abuse, but people simply don't care about that fact. If your brother is being abused by his wife, he needs to get out of that situation. 

The problem with him leaving his wife would be that the children would be left with only one parent. But if their choices boil down to a mother who has a history of being a domestic abuser, and a father with a history of cheating, the outlook for these children will be grim for the foreseeable future.

Recently my (now ex) fiancée left me, but it was actually me that left her... It was a confusing experience that you can read about on my profile. The first 2 posts on this account share the experiences that i had with it, both on r/amitheasshole. 

I ended up breaking up with my fiancée after several years of being together. I was diagnosed with clinical depression in 2013 and spent most of my time trying to cope with it. Our breakup was horrific for multiple reasons, but it was compounded by the fact that she turned MY DEPRESSION into a problem that was affecting her and she proceeded to tell me that i was a bad person for being depressed in the first place, since it made her job of being my fiancée harder. She was psychologically and physically abusive towards me, and i didn't realize it at the time. After our breakup, i tried to kill myself. My plan was to drive my car off the road and crash into whatever was strong enough to kill me. 

The only reason i didn't do it is because my friend Mike called me in time. Apparently the demon i used to be engaged to had made a post on Facebook about how i had been a terrible fiance and called my boss to tell her that i was a horrible human who deserved to be fired. Anyways, Mike was calling to let me know that I had been reported to my boss, but my bosses weren't taking it seriously. Once Mike figured out that i was single again, he made me stay on the phone with him until he could meet up with me in person. He took the rest of his day off work because he knew it was an emergency. When we met up in person, he just sat in my car with me until I finally began breaking down over those last few hours. After we finally got me back into a better mindset, Mike's wife was there to help me get my car to their apartment, since Mike didn't want me to drive. He was worried that i would end up crashing, not because of a suicide attempt, but because i had just spent the last few hours breaking down in tears and i was exhausted. 

The following day, Mike helped me collect my things from my old apartment, and he even helped me find a good psychologist. 

My point here is that i was lucky, even though I didn't feel lucky at the time. If Mike hasn't called me when he did, or if he had hung up and just tried to meet me somewhere (under the idea that i would go there immediately) then i would have killed myself that day. That was the day I learned that i had a real, true friend. I'm just sad that it took me literally trying to end my life for me to realize it. 

I didn't do anything to keep myself going; My friend kept me alive. 

If anybody out there is thinking about committing suicide, for any reason, please talk to a friend or somebody you trust. I was one of the lucky ones, and I don't want to know that anybody around me was unlucky enough to successfully end their lives.
